description: Shadow Mode results: pessimistic ShadowMatcher (realistic queue-position fills, taker slippage, Binance fee schedule) driven by live TOPOS topology decisions on real Binance BTCUSDT futures market data

runs.value_model_note: value model .so file was not present on this run (lost between sessions on the instance); engine correctly fell back to running without it, not a crash, but this run's decisions did not use the value_pred signal at all

consistent_finding_across_both_runs.maker_ratio: 0.0% in both independent sessions -- not a single limit order filled via queue exhaustion in either run
consistent_finding_across_both_runs.net_pnl: deeply negative in both runs, entirely driven by taker fees on a strategy that trades far more often than it should for its edge size
consistent_finding_across_both_runs.root_cause: LIQUIDITY_PROVISION logic places limit orders at exactly best bid/best ask with queue_position initialized to the FULL resting volume at that level (often 4-25 BTC observed in logs); at Binance BTCUSDT liquidity and trade sizes (fractions of a BTC per aggTrade), exhausting that queue takes far longer than the time between our own CANCEL_ALL triggers (which fire very frequently -- TOXIC_VORTEX/anomaly regime dominates the decision stream, consistent with the earlier Predictive Power Check finding that TOXIC_VORTEX was the most common labeled regime in a comparable session)
consistent_finding_across_both_runs.consequence: the strategy as currently implemented is a pure taker strategy in practice, despite being designed to alternate between maker and taker behavior by regime; it pays the 0.04% taker fee on every fill with no offsetting maker rebate income, on a directional signal (IMPULSE, from earlier validation) whose edge (~IC 0.42 at 10-tick horizon) is far too small and far too short-lived to cover round-trip taker fees plus the adverse selection of trading through an already-thin book

what_this_answers: the partner's original question -- 'does the signal survive contact with real execution economics' -- is now answered: NO, not with this execution logic. The infrastructure (WS dual-stream, lock-free AttractorBridge, spinlock-guarded OMS, pessimistic queue-position matcher) all functioned correctly and as designed. The trading logic layered on top of it (naive best-bid/best-ask posting, immediate CANCEL_ALL on every anomaly tick) is not economically viable against real Binance BTCUSDT liquidity and fee structure.
not_yet_investigated: whether posting further from best bid/ask (accepting worse queue position but avoiding constant cancel/repost churn) would improve maker fill rate
whether reducing CANCEL_ALL sensitivity (the anomaly threshold itself, separate from the refit cooldown already tuned) would reduce unnecessary order churn
whether the MARKET_TAKER logic's fixed tiny size (0.001 BTC) combined with the short-lived IMPULSE signal is fundamentally fee-negative regardless of tuning, given known IC decay past ~10-50 ticks

true unrealized mark-to-market PnL was not tracked during the session, only realized PnL from actual fills plus the final forced cancellation of any remaining open orders (which have no PnL impact since they never filled)

diagnostic_experiment_isolating_root_cau.hypothesis: is zero maker fill rate caused by CANCEL_ALL churn frequency (VORTEX regime firing too often to let orders wait), or by queue depth (resting volume too large relative to trade flow)?
diagnostic_experiment_isolating_root_cau.method: modified engine to suppress cancel_all specifically on VORTEX/anomaly decisions, letting maker limit orders ride through anomalies for the full 120s session (still force-canceled at shutdown, no PnL impact since unfilled)
diagnostic_experiment_isolating_root_cau.conclusion: hypothesis REJECTED for churn frequency: even with 358 potential premature cancellations suppressed (orders allowed to sit through anomaly regimes for the entire session), maker_ratio remained exactly 0.0%. This confirms the root cause is queue depth, not cancellation frequency -- the strategy joins the queue behind the full resting volume at best bid/ask (4-25 BTC observed), and realistic BTCUSDT aggTrade flow over these session lengths is insufficient to exhaust that queue regardless of how long the order is allowed to wait. Tuning CANCEL_ALL sensitivity or cooldown parameters will not fix maker fill rate; the order placement logic itself (posting at the very back of a deep queue) is the structural problem.
diagnostic_experiment_isolating_root_cau.implication_for_future_work: a maker strategy on this instrument/liquidity profile would need either much larger size relative to queue depth (capital-intensive and risky), joining thinner price levels further from best bid/ask (worse expected fill price if it does fill), or abandoning passive queue-joining in favor of a different maker mechanism entirely (e.g. quote inside the spread, accept adverse selection risk explicitly). This was not tested further; it is a separate, larger design question.
